payload.hypothesis: Connection churn from short Redis timeouts causes the leak
payload.conclusion: Redis timeout is not the cause
payload.text: Tried raising REDIS_TIMEOUT 200ms -> 800ms in config/redis.yml (commit 4a9f2c1). Memory still reached 2.1GB in 20 minutes under 1500 RPS load. Redis timeout is not the cause. Handing off to next shift — check Auth middleware.

payload.hypothesis: Redis connection pool exhaustion causes response buffer retention in worker memory
payload.action: Increased REDIS_MAX_CONNECTIONS 50 -> 250 and REDIS_KEEPALIVE 120s in config/redis.yml
payload.reason: Python worker RSS still reached 2.31GB in 18 minutes while Redis server memory stayed flat at 142MB
payload.conclusion: Redis connection pool size and keepalive do not affect the leak
payload.text: Increased REDIS_MAX_CONNECTIONS 50 -> 250 in config/redis.yml (commit 8c3d11e). Worker RSS still hit 2.31GB in 18m. Redis is completely ruled out. Heap dump points to 1.42M SessionContext objects in services/auth/auth_middleware.py.

payload.message: Run forced gc.collect(2) every 30s in payment worker loop

payload.hypothesis: Cyclic references in payment worker coroutines delay generation-2 garbage collection
payload.reason: Under light 200 RPS staging traffic, memory plateaued at 920MB
payload.conclusion: Aggressive GC sweep appeared to help at 200 RPS, needs high-load verification
payload.next_suspect: Verify GC sweep at 1500 RPS or inspect Auth middleware reference cycles
payload.text: Lowered GC_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SEC to 30s in services/payments/worker.py (commit c901b4f). At 200 RPS staging load, memory plateaued around 920MB.

payload.hypothesis: Cyclic references in payment worker coroutines delay generation-2 garbage collection
payload.action: Tested GC_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SEC=30s in services/payments/worker.py under 1800 RPS production replay
payload.reason: At 1800 RPS, forced gc.collect() caused p99 latency spikes to 1.9s and RSS still reached 2.2GB because _SESSION_CACHE holds strong references
payload.conclusion: Aggressive GC fails under production load because leaked objects are strongly referenced in Auth middleware
payload.text: Re-tested Devon's GC_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SEC=30s (commit d72e09a) at 1800 RPS prod replay. It failed: p99 spiked to 1.9s and memory still hit 2.2GB because _SESSION_CACHE holds strong dict references that GC cannot collect.

payload.message: Replace unbounded _SESSION_CACHE dict with bounded TTLCache(maxsize=50000, ttl=300)
payload.diff:
--- a/services/auth/auth_middleware.py
+++ b/services/auth/auth_middleware.py
@@ -18,3 +18,4 @@
-_SESSION_CACHE: dict[str, SessionContext] = {}
+_SESSION_CACHE = TTLCache(maxsize=50_000, ttl=300)

payload.hypothesis: Unbounded _SESSION_CACHE in auth_middleware.py retains SessionContext objects indefinitely on transient retry storms
payload.action: Replaced unbounded _SESSION_CACHE dict with TTLCache(maxsize=50000, ttl=300) in services/auth/auth_middleware.py
payload.reason: RSS stabilized at 480MB over a 2-hour 2,000 RPS soak test with zero OOMs
payload.conclusion: Unbounded Auth middleware session cache was the root cause of the memory leak
payload.next_suspect: None (resolved - roll out bounded TTLCache across all auth-middleware services)
payload.text: Replaced unbounded _SESSION_CACHE with TTLCache(maxsize=50000, ttl=300) in services/auth/auth_middleware.py (commit f31a88b). Memory held flat at 480MB for 2 hours at 2,000 RPS!

incidents.title: Auth Middleware JWKS Key Rotation Retry Storm

payload.hypothesis: Lowering JWKS HTTP timeout will clear stuck auth workers during IdP key rotation
payload.action: Lowered JWKS_FETCH_TIMEOUT from 2000ms to 250ms in services/auth/jwks_client.py
payload.reason: 250ms timeout triggered 8x synchronous retry amplification against IdP endpoint
payload.conclusion: Tightening JWKS timeout without singleflight coalescing worsens the retry storm
payload.next_suspect: Add singleflight lock + stale-while-revalidate caching in jwks_client.py
payload.text: Lowered JWKS_FETCH_TIMEOUT to 250ms (commit 7b2e19c). Failed: caused an 8x retry storm against the IdP. Next shift should implement singleflight coalescing in jwks_client.py.

incidents.title: Redis Sentinel Failover READONLY Stalled Writes

payload.hypothesis: Increasing Redis socket timeout will allow Sentinel failover to complete transparently
payload.action: Raised REDIS_TIMEOUT to 1500ms during Sentinel promotion
payload.reason: Pooled connections remained pinned to the demoted replica returning READONLY errors
payload.conclusion: Timeout tuning does not disconnect stale READONLY sockets; explicit disconnect_on_readonly=True is required
payload.text: Raising REDIS_TIMEOUT to 1500ms (commit 91a0e4d) did not recover stalled writes after Sentinel failover. Pooled connections stay pinned to the old replica.
